commentary_segments.text: For deep submicron CMOS the gain contributed by two transistors may not be sufficient. For MOSTs with gate lengths of 90 nm and less the gain of one single transistor is less than 10! To obtain more gain, feedback can be applied around the cascode transistor. It is then called a regulated cascode (Hosticka, Sackinger). This is also called gain boosting (Bult). This feedback is actually parallel-series feedback (see Chapter 8), causing the output impedance to rise by the amount of feedback gain. The gain goes up by the same amount. If we realize that feedback amplifier by just one transistor M3, the gain of that transistor is added to the total gain. An additional advantage of that feedback amplifier is that the impedance in the middle (at the gate of M3) is reduced by the same feedback gain.

source_conclusions.text: For deep submicron CMOS the gain contributed by two transistors may not be sufficient.
For MOSTs with gate lengths of 90 nm and less the gain of one single transistor is less than 10!
To obtain more gain, feedback can be applied around the cascode transistor.
This is also called gain boosting (Bult).
This feedback is actually parallel-series feedback (see Chapter 8), causing the output impedance to rise by the amount of feedback gain.
The gain goes up by the same amount.
If we realize that feedback amplifier by just one transistor M3, the gain of that transistor is added to the total gain.
An additional advantage of that feedback amplifier is that the impedance in the middle (at the gate of M3) is reduced by the same feedback gain.
